answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every identity must earn its standing by completing small verified jobs whose receipts are recorded in a shared atlas: each receipt is hash-linked to the last, so a newcomer cannot wander in with a bought reputation. New accounts must also lock a refundable deposit in a vault before they can transact, and one forged receipt slashes it. A thousand fake identities therefore cost a thousand deposits and a thousand verified jobs, so forgery pays less than honest work.
